e8596c4e95.q: What is the decommissioning process for data center equipment at Iron Mountain, from de-racking through disposition?
e8596c4e95.a: Iron Mountain begins planning with customers well before retirement through programmatic engagement. On decom day, the company performs site surveys, deploys proprietary data erasure solutions compliant with NIST standards, performs chain of custody tracking, de-racks equipment, provides secure transport to Iron Mountain facilities, then prioritizes reuse solutions at system level, component level, or open market sales. Assets that fail quality checks are processed through closed-loop recycling to recover critical materials and metals.
e8596c4e95.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware

0e9d50c2ac.q: How does Iron Mountain's decommissioning workflow differ between CPU server deployments and GPU-dense AI infrastructure?
0e9d50c2ac.a: At a high level, the workflow does not differ significantly. Iron Mountain has decades of experience producing reusable CPU components and systems for secondary markets. For GPU equipment, while the company does not yet have decades of experience, it is already seeing tremendous appetite for used GPU and AI equipment in secondary use. Tom Delahunty notes that GPU equipment is likely to follow the same longevity curve as CPU did, with increasing usable life extension observed over recent years.
0e9d50c2ac.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware

ff1185a05e.q: What operational challenges arise from liquid cooling in AI infrastructure during the decommissioning process?
ff1185a05e.a: GPU systems with liquid cooling are heavier and more valuable than air-cooled CPU systems, requiring additional handling steps to ensure proper management. Once equipment reaches Iron Mountain facilities, the core processes remain the same, but the company needs significantly more power and cooling distribution units to handle the cooling element of systems. As racks scale from 12-15 kilowatts to 100 kilowatts and beyond, only a limited number of companies have the infrastructure capability to test such systems, which Iron Mountain plans to build out worldwide.
ff1185a05e.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware

9670523410.q: What growth metrics did Iron Mountain's asset lifecycle division achieve in Q2 and Q4 2025?
9670523410.a: Iron Mountain recorded approximately 70% year-over-year growth in Q4 2025. In Q2, the asset lifecycle division achieved plus 88% year-over-year growth and plus 82% organic growth, driven by tremendous volume of assets coming to end-of-use in the data center and AI space as customers require secure, scalable solutions for large-volume asset decommissioning.
9670523410.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware

8b1f97dd3f.q: What drives increasing customer acceptance of used and refurbished GPU and AI equipment in secondary markets?
8b1f97dd3f.a: Tom Delahunty attributes the shift primarily to necessity rather than education. Supply chain shortages cascading through the industry, particularly for silicon and GPU supply, have forced customers to deploy used equipment. This necessity is now generating test cases, use cases, and case studies that build acceptance and adoption of used equipment, which Delahunty believes will serve the industry well beyond current supply chain shortages for decades to come.
8b1f97dd3f.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware

95845c32a1.q: What infrastructure and R&D investments does Iron Mountain believe the ITAD industry needs to handle future AI hardware volumes?
95845c32a1.a: Tom Delahunty states that the ITAD industry is under-invested in research and development for new solutions, more efficient processing, better logistics, and critical mineral recovery. He argues that only a limited number of large companies will have the capability to build out the infrastructure to meet the unique demands of AI equipment and the massive volume anticipated in coming years. Iron Mountain is investing in R&D for reuse solutions, efficient processing, logistics optimization, and partnerships to unlock critical minerals from recycled components.
95845c32a1.e: The Circular Supply Chain for AI Hardware
